expected_title: Design of a Zero-Gravity, Vacuum-Based 3D Printer Robot for Use of In-Space Satellite Assembly
abstract: Additive manufacturing has revolutionized many industries through its ability to print unique architectures impossible to create with traditional subtractive manufacturing. The space environment, given its condition of microgravity and vacuum, creates unique challenges for most additive methods, but also an exceptional opportunity. This paper explores the application of additive manufacturing (or 3D printing) in this new environment, and introduces design opportunities for a printing robot for such application of satellite assembly on-orbit. The ability to print both long, simple booms and large, flat structures like an antenna dish will be pursued. This capability will help reduce structural limitations due to the launch environment and allow for unique satellite architectures outside the boundaries of a launch vehicle payload fairing. From a systems engineering viewpoint, the mission and system requirements and initial design specifications will be discussed and integration of the 3D printer capability on the robot will detailed.
